item.title: Euronews: Ex-German intelligence chief arrested over suspected espionage
item.description: Former BND president August Hanning is accused of obtaining classified documents from his former agency, with investigators reportedly examining whether information was passed to foreign powers.

item.title: Euronews: Latvian filmmaker wins €400,000 Grand Prix at Kazakhstan's AI film festival
item.description: The first Astana AI Film Festival has concluded in Kazakhstan, with Latvian filmmaker Nikolay Shestak taking the Grand Prix. The festival had a total fund of €1.8 million, with half allocated to prize money and the other half to investment in promising AI teams and film production in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Euronews: MEP Lena Schilling describes ‘immense shock’ after finding nude deepfakes of herself
item.description: Green MEP Lena Schilling has described nude deepfake images of herself and several other MEPs as “unacceptable”, saying their creators tried to take her “dignity away”.

item.title: POLITICO Europe: Von der Leyen warns against EU budget cuts
item.description: Commission president dismissed Germany's calls for big savings, arguing that they would undermine EU-wide priorities.

item.title: Euronews: Faster returns and stricter border controls: How the EU plans to tighten migration
item.description: The EU is cracking down on migration two months after launching the Migration and Asylum Pact. Migrants with no right to stay must leave and may be transferred to “return hubs”. A new European Return Order will include key elements of return decisions. But is the EU prepared?

item.title: Euronews: Global oil stocks are alarmingly low and could take two years to rebuild, Aramco warns
item.description: The CEO of the world's biggest oil company warned at a conference that the global oil supply system is reaching its limit and that replenishing global oil stockpiles could take two years.

item.title: Euronews: Turkey and Pakistan to send troops to Saudi Arabia under defence pact
item.description: The three signatories of the August Mecca Joint Defence Agreement met in emergency session in Riyadh and agreed to move immediately to "rapid deployment" of military forces, uniting NATO's second-largest army, the Islamic world's only nuclear state and the largest Gulf power.

item.title: Euronews: Sánchez able 'to convert' housing weakness 'into strenght', expert says
item.description: Javier Carbonell, an analyst at the European Policy Centre, says that while housing has been one of the “biggest policy failures” of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s administration, the prime minister has been able to turn it into an electoral issue.

item.title: Euronews: Tear gas and water cannon in Pristina as protesters clash with police
item.description: Police fired tear gas as protesters clashed outside Kosovo’s parliament over moves to limit powers of a Hague war crimes court.

item.title: Euronews: Drones hit two ships off coast of Bulgaria, sinking one, as government calls emergency meeting
item.description: A search is under way for the missing crew, with no one yet blamed for what is reported to be the first attack on shipping in the NATO member's economic zone.

item.title: Euronews: Jeffrey Archer, bestselling British novelist and disgraced politician, dies aged 86
item.description: Archer was a disgraced politician and convicted liar but found success as novelist. His books are estimated to have sold more than 300 million copies worldwide.

item.title: Euronews: Germany's far-right AfD bids to take helm of state parliament in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: The outcome hinges on five deputies from the BSW party, in a vote seen as a first test of relations between the two before the AfD's bid to lead the state government in December.

item.title: Euronews: Fuel in Italy, tax cuts expire: diesel prices rise as hauliers threaten strikes
item.description: With tax breaks expiring and delay to the variable excise decree, diesel prices climb. Hauliers warn of a strike as the government summons oil firms with initial price caps.

item.title: Euronews: Housing protest turns violent in Barcelona with fires and arrests
item.description: Barcelona’s housing protest turned violent with fires and arrests, highlighting Spain’s affordability crisis ahead of a general strike and snap election in November.

item.title: Euronews: Barcelona housing protest erupts into clashes as barricades burn
item.description: Protests over housing rights ended in serious unrest in central Barcelona, with barricades and burning bins. Catalan police arrested 13 people, and 30 officers suffered minor injuries.

item.title: Euronews: With Pedro Sánchez at the helm, Spain’s socialist stronghold is cracking
item.description: Good morning. It’s Tuesday, and my name is Angela Skujins. On today’s docket: election tremors in Spain, combating sexualised deepfakes, and how Brussels bigwigs plan to thwart the bloc’s ‘Trojan horses’.

item.title: Euronews: Joana Vasconcelos blends art and haute couture in exhibition for Valentino Garavani
item.description: Lisbon is hosting an exhibition where works by sculptor Joana Vasconcelos converse with dresses by a renowned Italian designer, fusing domestic life and haute couture.

item.title: Euronews: Kosovo police use tear gas on protesters demanding curbs on war crimes court
item.description: Anger has been building since former president Hashim Thaci, viewed by many as a hero of the independence struggle, was sentenced last month over crimes committed during the 1990s war against Serbia.

item.title: Euronews: Europe Today: Sánchez calls snap election in Spain as French students protest again
item.description: Pedro Sánchez is gambling on a snap election on 29 November, after Congress rejected his housing decrees and tens of thousands protested. In France, students take to the streets again over overcrowded classes and teacher shortages, while MEPs debate Europe's housing crisis and AI deepfakes.

item.title: Euronews: France's sovereign debt crisis explained: How dangerous could it be?
item.description: French borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2002, and the gap with Germany is the widest since 2011. What is driving France's debt crisis and how far could it go?

item.title: Euronews: Ronaldo’s next chapter: What lies ahead after Portugal’s Nations League progress?
item.description: By beating Norway 2-1, Portugal reached the Nations League quarter-finals and a new squad list is expected. The question everyone asks is: and Cristiano Ronaldo?

item.title: Euronews: Could teenage fitness shape your mental health decades later? New research suggests it might
item.description: Being fit as a teenager may help protect against depression in adulthood, a new study suggests.

item.title: Euronews: Simpler itineraries, longer stays: How travellers embrace doing less while on holiday
item.description: From slower, less-planned breaks to AI scepticism and the rise of nearby escapes, travellers are expected to prioritise deeper and more meaningful experiences in 2027.

item.title: Euronews: Latest news bulletin | October 6th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Euronews: EU mulls tougher restrictions on Russian diplomats as hybrid threats intensify
item.description: The recent spate of hybrid attacks across Europe has raised questions over the possible involvement of Russian diplomats, prompting member states to consider tighter restrictions and checks.

item.title: Euronews: Quebec separatists vow independence referendum after winning local elections but falling short of majority
item.description: Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has pledged to work with the incoming separatist government in Quebec to address the needs and issues of the province, including resisting a hostile US administration, creating jobs and building housing.

item.title: Euronews: Fake NATO deaths, Epstein claims and drones: how Russia targets elections in the Baltics
item.description: Russia-linked disinformation campaigns targeting elections in Estonia and Latvia have focused less on individual candidates or the voting process itself and more on sowing confusion around the security issues shaping voters’ decisions, according to a new report.

item.title: Euronews: Police braces for nationwide day of protests across French high schools demanding reforms and more resources
item.description: Students are demanding the government address issues they view as critical to their education, including upgrading classroom facilities, ensuring schools in less economically affluent areas are not disadvantaged, as well as reforms to the school system and the long hours pupils spend in schools.

item.title: Euronews: Musical residencies: Business is booming, but who pays the most for pop stars playing in Europe?
item.description: Musical residencies are on the rise in Europe for major pop stars, but costs are increasingly being heaped upon audiences with travel, accommodation and extras pushing up ticket prices, according to Spanish consumer rights group FACUA.

item.title: Euronews: Climate damage already ‘locked in’ – but these 10 insights show our future is still being decided
item.description: From rising sea levels to food systems fuelling climate change – experts have laid out 10 insights that require urgent action.
